one_liner: C++20 embedded transactional KV store (radix trie, node-level COW) with a RocksDB-API shim; 1.6-3x RocksDB on bank transfers.
what_it_does: PsiTri is a persistent, transactional, embedded key-value store. The repo is still named arbtrie. It is memory-mapped, gives MVCC snapshot isolation, has 512 independent top-level roots, can store whole subtrees as values, and supports O(log n) range count and range delete. The native API is its own C++20 interface: a database handle, thread-affine write/read sessions, and transactions with upsert/get/commit plus cursors. Compatibility shims ship alongside it: PsiTriRocks reimplements a subset of the rocksdb/*.h headers, so you relink against psitri::psitrirocks instead of RocksDB. There are also MDBX and LevelDB shims, and an optional SQLite shim.
how_it_is_fast: The index is an adaptive radix trie crossed with a B-tree. Inner nodes route on 1-byte dividers found with a SIMD lower_bound (NEON, SSE2/SSSE3 or AVX-512, chosen at compile time), and leaves are sorted ~2 KB nodes with hash-accelerated lookup. Copy-on-write happens per node in 64-byte multiples instead of 4 KB pages. Every object is reached through a 32-bit ID in a control-block table, so the segment allocator (SAL) can move an object with a memcpy plus one CAS, while writers bump-allocate in private 32 MB segments. The DWAL write path puts commits into a writer-private in-memory ART buffer plus a buffered WAL append with no fsync. Two background merge threads then drain 100K-entry batches into the COW trie, so there is no LSM compaction and readers get lock-free MVCC snapshots.
when_to_use: Small read-modify-write transactions (ledger or balance updates, blockchain or game state) that touch a few keys atomically, where durability via a periodic flush is acceptable instead of an fsync per commit.
One writer plus concurrent point readers that need consistent snapshots. In the bank runs, native PsiTri's write throughput did not drop with a reader attached (+1.5% on M5 Max, +10.7% on EPYC).
A RocksDB app that only uses Put/Get/Delete/WriteBatch/iterators/snapshots on the default column family and wants to try another engine by relinking.
Workloads that count or delete key ranges often, or that store hierarchical data (nested subtrees, O(1) snapshot of a subtree).
Linux or macOS on x86-64 or ARM64 with a dataset up to about 2x RAM. The scale benchmark held >300K inserts/s and >11M reads/s (12 threads) up to that point.
when_not_to_use: You need durability on every commit. All published benchmarks use sync=none, and unflushed DWAL WAL entries are lost on crash. PsiTriRocks ignores WriteOptions::sync and Options::use_fsync; only Flush() syncs the WAL.

Disk space is tight. Data is never compressed, and files run 2-4x the live data under sustained writes: 1,088 MB for PsiTri vs 320 MB for RocksDB in the M5 bank run, and 76.7 GB vs 51.5 GB at 200M random upserts.
Your code depends on RocksDB merge operators, bloom filters, block cache, compression, statistics or compaction tuning. PsiTriRocks accepts these silently and ignores them, and Merge behaves as Put.
Scan-heavy or bulk-load-heavy work. MDBX scanned 2-4x faster in the bank runs, and RocksDB bulk-loaded faster than PsiTriRocks on both machines (1.96M vs 1.80M and 1.16M vs 0.96M ops/s).

You need a proven production engine. It is pre-1.0 (the authors say the API may change and it is not battle-tested), has 4 stars and no independent replication, and native PsiTri lost to MDBX on the x86 VM (164K vs 239K transfers/s). Writes to the same root are serialized by a mutex.

integration.dependencies: Threads plus in-repo libraries (sal, ucc, art, hash, bundled xxhash). A standalone build also requires Boost.program_options, Catch2 3 (tests are on by default) and fetches abseil via CMake FetchContent; PsiTriRocks links absl::btree privately. The SQLite and DuckDB layers are optional.
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 and CMake 3.16+. The README says Clang 15+ or GCC 12+, but the top-level CMakeLists states that LLVM clang is required and GCC is not supported, and on macOS it hard-codes Homebrew LLVM's clang++. The benchmarks used Clang 17 and Clang 20.
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS (POSIX mmap/mlock; no Windows code path found). Runs on x86-64 (SSE2/SSSE3/AVX-512 paths) and ARM64 (NEON), with scalar fallbacks. -march=native is on by default, so binaries are not portable unless you turn it off. CI runs on Ubuntu only.
integration.thread_safety: The database handle is thread-safe. Sessions are thread-affine: create each one on the thread that uses it, with at most 50 application write sessions of 32 MB each. Each of the 512 roots allows one writer at a time, and writes to the same root are serialized by a mutex. Readers use lock-free MVCC snapshots, except that the 'latest' read mode, which PsiTriRocks uses for Get, takes a shared lock against the writer.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — source-compatible only. PsiTri ships its own subset of the rocksdb/*.h headers, so you relink to psitri::psitrirocks; it is not ABI-compatible and cannot open existing RocksDB data directories, since it uses its own on-disk format. Put/Get/MultiGet/Delete/DeleteRange/WriteBatch/iterators/snapshots and up to 512 column families work. Merge becomes Put; bloom filters, cache, compression, statistics, compaction options and WAL options are ignored; Iterator::Refresh returns NotSupported.

gotchas: In PsiTriRocks, WriteBatch drops the column-family argument (Put(cf, k, v) forwards to Put(k, v)), and DB::Write always writes to root 0, so column-family writes made through a batch land in the default column family.

OpenForReadOnly just calls Open, which opens the database read-write. Flush() and CompactRange() are accepted but only sync the WAL or do nothing; to reclaim disk space you must call compact_and_truncate (the psitri.compact_and_truncate property through the shim).

Long-lived snapshots compete with live nodes for cacheline slots, and inner-node fan-out can drop from 256 to as low as 16 until they are released. Recovery after a crash scans the whole database, which the docs estimate at minutes for a 100 GB database.

Write sessions are heavy (32 MB buffer each, backed by thread_local storage). Do not create them per request or pass them between threads. DWAL merges also stall: in the 200M-key random-upsert run the minimum round throughput was 24,791 ops/s, vs 85,161 for RocksDB.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PsiTri over SplinterDB, KVell or F2 when the workload is small multi-key atomic transactions with concurrent readers that need snapshots. Those siblings' catalogued wins measure raw insert or lookup throughput, while PsiTri's evidence is on transactions. If you rely on merge operators, compression or bloom filters, or need to reopen existing RocksDB data, prefer an engine that keeps RocksDB's feature set and format, because PsiTriRocks drops them.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own TPC-B-style bank benchmark counts 5 KV ops per atomic transfer, uses triangular skew and runs with sync=none. At batch=1 on an 8-core AMD EPYC-Turin Vultr VM (Clang 20, -O3 -flto -march=native), the RocksDB-API shim PsiTriRocks wrote 2.3x as many transfers/s as RocksDB (369K vs 158K), and its concurrent reader did 4.9x as many reads/s (1.42M vs 290K). At batch=100, native PsiTri was about 2.98x RocksDB 9.9.3 on an Apple M5 Max (Clang 17, -O3 -flto=thin) but only about 1.57x on the EPYC VM, where MDBX (239K) and TidesDB (167K) beat it (164K).
status_note: The project is actively developed but pre-1.0: the last main commit (2026-04-28) was one of a burst of MVCC and recovery fixes, the repo has 4 stars and is still named arbtrie, and it is MIT-licensed and installable as a CMake static library, though the authors warn the API may change and it has no production track record.
